evidence: Row 17 asks for plausible implementation coverage, not an Oracle score. No missing required screen, role or flow was found. All task paths below are under .qc-cache/hireops-2026-10-01-transaction-hardening-r2/task/; src/ and public/ paths are relative to solution/app/. instruction.md:1-13 and environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md sections 1-11 were mapped to the reference. public/js/app.js:13-20 and public/js/hireops.js:44-419 implement Requisitions, Offers, Equity, Referrals and readable Audit, with public/js/change-sets.js:2-92 adding Coordinated Changes, an ordinary 2-4-member editor, durable preview/history, commit and original-receipt retrieval. public/index.html:18-33 and src/index.js:70-115 provide the seven supplied session identities; src/index.js:308-408 applies role, tier, dual-control and current-leaf authorization to offer creation/approval/revision/rescission. src/rules.js:24-149 implements strict UTC dates, original-anchor calendar months, exact BigInt ratios, both compensation totals, separate vesting schedules and fixed-clock referrals; lines 154-181 derive headroom and signing-history net from movements. src/index.js:328-402 wraps each settlement and receipt in a SQLite transaction; revisions preserve predecessor history, replace grants and post signed differences, and rescission uses the latest offer with original dates. src/change-sets.js:22-64 validates complete canonical intent and final net budgets, :77-104 stores immutable previews and rejects touched-ledger ABA/stale leaves, and :105-140 posts every member and batch receipt atomically. Cached commits return the original stored result after current-session authorization (:94-98). public/js/app.js:193-205 and public/js/change-sets.js:31-36,78-84 retain failed revision/rescission/change inputs. public/js/hireops.js:121-168,264-319,321-415 exposes compensation, payments, historical grants, referral halves/cliff and expandable immutable before/after receipts. src/db.js:122-179 seeds once; bootstrap.js:18-45 serves DB-independent health and honors PORT; db.js:13-28 honors DB_PATH and uses bundled seed. Raw evidence index SHA256 c329efb36f03a5835d8c2d3a23b21f197d84df28466a09f205211b0a2849a1df contained 135 entries, all verified with no mismatches. local/targeted-golden/results.json SHA256 ca0591e4a2ed5f03108868b5e56ecd08e3eb82776adf5cebb6f9323c2a077bf2 binds all 14 solution files to current frozen bytes and records 3 successful browser groups; its driver lines 30-66 actually asserts refusal retention, corrected commit and rendered grant/payment/referral facts. local/archive-batch-domain/results.json SHA256 a44c0bf81b27981d9bf1d63239f8b7ce7da5733d6d70aef425e2350a76b7732f records 15 successful finite HTTP groups; the reviewed batch-domain.cjs assertions cover netted cycles, complete rollback, receipt retries, overlapping/disjoint previews and restart. local/install-lifecycle/results.json SHA256 52b5ba96bded2e133fe4ec16117c150d46673f70ce31284169193f478c73e9f9 also binds all 13 app files and records actual process replacement retaining data. These finite observations support coverage; full configured grade, workload, reward-ordering and Oracle/target scores remain unmeasured and are outside this row verdict.
counterexample: A superficially complete desk could validate freshness only by headroom balance, accept an ABA-stale preview, or check each move against intermediate headroom and reject a fully funded exchange. The actual golden has ledger-identity freshness and final-net calculation; the reviewed batch-witnesses.cjs changes exactly those behaviors, and local/batch-witnesses/results.json (SHA256 477ba650c81ce00e5d6346f679b774f23c5a197b78b346bb183e7eb0a70bcf83) records the balance-only variant returning 200 instead of 409 and sequential-budget variant refusing the valid cycle, while golden passes all 15 groups. Conversely, an app starting with no operational demonstration rows is explicitly conforming (instruction.md:11 and rules section 1); the empty_operational_seed variant passes the same 15 groups. This review does not require imported demo history, exact routes, labels or generated IDs.
